title: What you believe
hook: Judaism has room for many beliefs; write yours honestly
tomorrow: belief is half of it. which of the things you do are yours?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a candle or a l'chaim, and a memory that blesses. Remember well. Now a new stretch, your own path, and it starts with what you hold true.

College roommate forms ask the oddest things. Night owl or early bird. Neat or messy. And at the bottom of Noa's: anything about your beliefs we should know? One blank box. Where would anyone start? Jewish tradition has an old answer, and it begins with a gesture: a hand over the eyes.
screen: `NIGHT OWL OR EARLY BIRD?` → `ONE BLANK BOX.` → `A HAND OVER THE EYES.`

segments.voice: The line is the Shema: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." The Talmud tells that Rabbi Judah the Prince passed his hand over his eyes when he said it, and people still cover their eyes for that line. It's the center: shut out the noise, say the one thing. But around that center, Judaism has argued about belief for a long time. Maimonides set out principles of faith in his commentary on the Mishnah. Later thinkers, Joseph Albo among them, pushed back and drew up a different list. When two great schools of sages disagreed, the Talmud said of them both: these and these are the words of the living God. So the tradition gives a center and a wide, argued-over room around it. Writing your beliefs honestly fits that room. Some will be firm, some brand new, some still being tested. Something to tell a friend tonight: covering your eyes for the Shema goes back to one line about one rabbi's hand.
screen: `HEAR, O ISRAEL: THE LORD IS ONE.` · `A HAND OVER THE EYES.` · `MAIMONIDES' LIST, AND ITS CRITICS.` · `THESE AND THESE.` · then, large: `YOUR BELIEFS.`

segments.voice: Cover your eyes with one hand, the way people do for the Shema, and stay there for a few slow breaths. Then, on paper and by hand, write three sentences that start with "I believe": one you're sure of, one you're growing into, one you're still testing.
screen: `A HAND OVER THE EYES.` · `THREE LINES: I BELIEVE.` · `SURE, GROWING, TESTING.`

segments.voice: What you believe: the things you hold true, written honestly, around the Shema's center and in the tradition's wide room.
For the road: your beliefs, half-sure ones included. That's day one of your own path.
